The evidence collectively shows that age requirements depend on the type of permit and jurisdiction. However, Pennsylvania state law allows individuals 18 or older to possess firearms under supervision or for specific activities like hunting [d1, d8], and those aged 18-20 may apply for a License to Carry under certain conditions [d4]. For purchasing, federal law requires being 21 for handguns from licensed dealers and 18 for long guns [d3]. Local permits, like in Erie County, New York, require applicants to be at least 21 [d5]. In Pennsylvania, the age to get a gun permit varies by permit type. For a standard License to Carry Firearms, which allows concealed carry, you must be at least 21 years old [d7, d8]. However, individuals aged 18-20 in Pennsylvania may be able to obtain a License to Carry under certain conditions, as indicated by a recent Reddit discussion citing state police policy [d4]. For purchasing firearms, federal law requires a person to be 21 to buy a handgun from a licensed dealer and 18 to buy a long gun [d3]. Additionally, Pennsylvania offers a Sportsman's Firearm Permit for those 18 or older who are licensed to hunt or fish [d8]. Requirements can also differ by county, as seen in Erie County, New York, where a pistol permit requires the applicant to be at least 21 [d5].
